I've delegated all three orders to demo-builder at a budget of 150,000 each. None of them has been built yet; they are waiting in the builder's queue in this order:

| Order | Lesson | Message | Stage |
|---|---|---|---|
| O-1 | one-metre-more-rope | M-4 | build |
| O-2 | three-sticks-one-triangle | M-5 | build |
| O-3 | four-cards-one-rule | M-6 | build |

**Split:** the roster in ORG.md lists only one builder, demo-builder, so all three went to it. They work well as one run anyway: they're from the same group of geometry lessons (brief `math.geometry.md`), and none waits on another (no `--after`), so one session can work through them in sequence.

**What confused me:**
- **Budget mismatch:** O-1's order carries a budget of 3,000,000, but I delegated at 150,000 as you instructed. I didn't check the order budgets for O-2 and O-3. If 150,000 is too small for a full build, the builder could run out partway.
- **Finding the builder:** the prompt says "your builders", but no command lists who reports to a manager. I found demo-builder in ORG.md's roster.

why: `<a command the guard cannot read>` is not allowed in an agent session (deploys need the founder's approval; pushing, publishing and verifying claims are code's or a person's)

said:
I built all 3 queued lessons and handed each in to test1. The queue is now empty and the session is closed. Each one passes `npm run check` (no errors for its slug), `tsc` and a production `next build`. `tools/reveal-fit.mjs` at 390×844 gives each a verdict of fit with stage-top crop 0 px. I did not run the official QA: that is code's qa stage. Every claim is `unverified`, status is `review`, and each has `design.md` plus `build.md` with `## Pre-flight v1`.

| Item | Lesson | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| O-1 | `math/one-metre-more-rope` | Handed in. A zoom window drawn at one scale for every circle, with a 20 cm ruler, so the Earth's top looks flat honestly. Gap is 15.9 cm for ball, wheel and Earth. Reveal 74 words (tool count). |
| O-2 | `math/three-sticks-one-triangle` | Handed in. Hinged sticks with the gap worked out from the angles: 2.6 / 1.0 / 3.6 cm at 45° / 0° / 60°. 3, 4, 6 closes; 2, 4, 6 shows "height 0". Reveal 81 words. |
| O-3 | `math/four-cards-one-rule` | Handed in. Four card buttons, each showing its two possible backs tagged "breaks" or "fine". Reveal 79 words. |

**Choices I made where the brief was silent** (each one is in that lesson's `build.md` for cm-math):
- **Predict questions:** in all three I added a second-person opening and stated the condition the answer depends on. The biggest is "each card has a letter on one side and a number on the other" in the four-cards lesson.
- **Traces after Reset:** chips keep a tick and the gap they showed (✓ 15.9 cm), so Reset can't erase what the reveal quotes. In the four-cards lesson the backs reappear when the reveal opens, and Reset is disabled then. This takes the rope lesson to 20 stage words against the brief's 17, and the sticks lesson to 14 against 13. Both stay under 25.
- **Sticks lesson:** "Lay them flat" and "Raise them" only apply to the 2, 3, 6 set. Pressed on another set, they bring 2, 3, 6 back.
- **Rope lesson:** the cat clause is kept as claim c4. Per the brief, the fact-checker may withdraw it, and then the clause gets cut.
- **Rope lesson, window size:** the zoom window is 340×200, not the brief's 340×180, so the lifted rope over the Earth clears the icon.

**What confused me:**
- `meta.mjs check --order=O-1` failed with "no *.test.mjs". It is a generic test runner that looks for test files at the worktree root, and these orders had no `checks`, so I treated it as not applicable.
- `next build` rewrites `tsconfig.json` (it adds the dist dir to `include`). I reverted it each time.
- A new lesson only gets built after `npm run registry` (or `npm run typecheck`) regenerates the index files. I hit this on O-2 and had to rebuild.
- On a 390 px phone the side rail narrows the stage to about 288 px, so SVG text renders at 0.847 scale. Labels needed 12 px in the viewBox to stay at the 10 px floor.
- The protection hook blocks a whole Bash command if any part of it touches a protected path, even a read-only grep of `src/kit/Lesson.tsx`. That also stopped an unrelated `sed` in the same command; I re-ran it on its own.

I fact-checked three lessons: one goes back to the builder, two passed. The session then closed because the queue was empty (3 items of a cap of 4).

1. **one-metre-more-rope: revise** (goes back to build). Three claims are verified: circumference = 2πr; the gap is 0.159155 m (15.9 cm) for all three radii, which I recomputed; and the Earth's radius, from WGS 84's a = 6,378,137 m, confirmed through the EPSG registry ([epsg.io](https://epsg.io/7661); I couldn't reach NGA's own document). Two findings:
   - **The cat claim is disputed.** "Enough for a cat to crawl under" is labelled as resting on a definition, with no source. A 2024 study by Pongrácz reports an average cat is 19.61 cm tall lying down and 27.97 cm at the shoulder, so it may not fit under a 15.9 cm gap ([Smithsonian](https://www.smithsonianmag.com/smart-news/cats-may-be-aware-of-their-body-size-suggests-study-of-their-famously-liquid-behavior-180985282/), [ScienceAlert](https://www.sciencealert.com/cats-basically-are-a-liquid-after-all-study-confirms)). The builder should cut the clause or give it a cited measurement.
   - **Minor:** the recall question uses a running track, which is not a circle, while the claim only covers circles. The 32 cm answer is still right. The builder should either make the recall object a circle or widen the claim to cover the track.
2. **three-sticks-one-triangle: pass**, all 3 claims verified, moves on to the learner review. The 2, 3, 6 cm sticks never get closer than 1 cm at any pair of angles, not just the preset ones. The 2.6, 3.6 and 1.0 cm readouts and the 3, 4, 6 corner point all recompute correctly.
3. **four-cards-one-rule: pass**, both claims verified, moves on to the learner review. I checked the truth table, and listed every letter and digit as a possible back: only E and 7 can break the rule.

Each record is at `company/reviews/<slug>/2026-10-22-fact-check.md` in that lesson's own worktree.

Two things confused me:
- The launch prompt named only the one-metre-more-rope worktree, but `room next` gave me items with their own worktrees. I worked each one in the worktree its pack named.
- The proxy blocked fetching the Smithsonian page, so the study figures come from search-result summaries rather than the paper itself. It didn't change the outcome, because the cat claim has no source either way.

I reviewed two lessons as the learner-evaluator and passed both with verdict **launch**. Both went on to the launch stage, and then the queue was empty, so the session closed at 2 of the 4 allowed items.

**1. three-sticks-one-triangle (O-2, v1)**
- **Review:** `company/reviews/three-sticks-one-triangle/2026-10-22-learner-knows-triangle-has-three-sides.md`
- **Why it works:** laying the sticks flat (gap 1.0 cm) shows on screen that even the best case falls short. Raising them makes the gap wider (2.6 cm, then 3.6 cm), so tilting is ruled out too.
- **I checked the gap numbers myself and they are right:** 2.564 rounds to 2.6 and 3.606 to 3.6.
- **Notes, none blocking:**
  - The sticks are only ever shown at equal angles, so a learner might still wonder about tilting them unequally.
  - "the detour" in the reveal is never explained.
  - "gap 0.0 cm" next to a filled triangle reads a little oddly.

**2. four-cards-one-rule (O-3, v1)**
- **Review:** `company/reviews/four-cards-one-rule/2026-10-22-learner-knows-everyday-if-then.md`
- **Why it works:** tapping the tempting 4 card shows both possible backs marked "fine", so the learner sees for themselves that it can't break the rule. The reveal then answers exactly the wrong pick.
- **Notes, none blocking:**
  - P and Q are never linked to "shows a vowel" and "back is even".
  - The reveal explains why the 4 is useless but not why the K is.
  - The small back tiles reuse the cards' own symbols (4, 7, K), which can confuse at a glance.
  - The lesson never says the possible backs are limited to 4 or 7 and A or K.

**What confused me**
- **Version number:** the review template needs a `lesson version: v<N>` line, but I wasn't allowed to read `meta.json`. I wrote v1 and ran the stage's own checker (`learner-verdict.mjs`) before handing in; it confirmed v1 for both.
- **Two verdict words:** `room next` only accepts pass or revise, while the review file must say launch, revise or fatal. I handed in "pass" alongside reviews that say "launch".
- **Second item's location:** it came with its own worktree (`.../worktrees/LESSON-four-cards-one-rule`), so I wrote that review there, not in the first item's directory.
- **Other files in the reviews folders:** both already held the fact-check, QA, build and design records. I didn't open them.

I fixed both fact-check findings on **LESSON-one-metre-more-rope (O-1)**, and the lesson is now v2. It has moved on to test1. The queue was empty after it, so the session is closed.

- **A1 (cat clause):** the fact-checker found the reveal's "enough for a cat to crawl under" was unsourced and wrong (cats are taller than 15.9 cm even lying down). I cut the clause from the reveal in `Demo.tsx` and deleted claim c4 from `meta.json`, which the brief allows. I didn't mark c4 `withdrawn`, because a builder may only set `unverified`.
- **B2 (recall):** the recall used a running track, which isn't a circle, so claim c2 didn't cover it. The object is now "a giant round water tank", and the explanation says "however big the tank". The answer is still "About 32 cm", which c2 already covers.
- **Claims c1–c3:** wording unchanged. I set them back to `unverified` and removed `checkedBy`, `checkedOn` and the fact-checker's notes, since they were verified during this order.
- **Records:** `meta.version` is 2. `build.md` has a "Revise v2" section and `## Pre-flight v2`, and `design.md` has the v2 changes.

`npm run check` shows no errors for this slug (the errors it prints are about other, already-published lessons) and `tsc --noEmit` passes. I didn't re-run the phone-fit tool: the reveal only got shorter and the stage is unchanged, and the qa stage re-runs it.

One thing confused me: `meta.mjs check --order=O-1` returned `pass:false` because it found no `*.test.mjs` files in the worktree. It seems to run the builder's own tests, which a lesson order doesn't have, while test1 for this flow runs the company's build gate. Test1 passed v1 without any such tests, so I treated it as not applying and recorded this in `--learned`.

I chaired two launch reviews and gave both lessons **go**. Both have moved on to the ship gates, and the session ended because the queue was empty.

1. **three-sticks-one-triangle v1 (O-2): go.** I read the walkthrough first and recomputed the gap readouts myself: 1.0 cm lying flat, 2.6 cm at 45° and 3.6 cm at 60°. They match the screen and the fact-checker's verified claims. The QA and learner reviews (verdict: launch) are both on file. Five objections travel with it: no analytics-steward predictions until M7, no accessibility review (advisory only), the learning-designer merged into the builder (F-f), the learner reviewer's non-blocking notes, and `evidence.simulatedLearner` left empty in meta.json.
   - Record: `company/rituals/records/2026-10-22-launch-review-three-sticks-one-triangle.md`
2. **four-cards-one-rule v1 (O-3): go.** The "breaks"/"fine" tags on the stage match the brief's enumeration, and the fact-checker checked the claim over every digit and letter, not just the stage's two possible backs. Six objections travel with it: the same three carried ones, the learner reviewer's notes, the fact-checker's wording point about the 4, and the same unlinked review in meta.json. The learner note most worth acting on in a v2 is that the reveal never says why K is useless.
   - Record: `company/rituals/records/2026-10-22-launch-review-four-cards-one-rule.md`

Two things confused me:
- **Template vs. checked format:** the launch-review template offers "go with conditions" and asks for a committed-predictions table. Your brief rules out conditions and defers predictions to M7, so I wrote "None" there and listed the gap as an objection.
- **Learner review not linked:** in both lessons, meta.json lists no simulated-learner review even though one exists for v1. As a result, the trust sheet shows "0 simulated-learner reviews" (it was also recorded before the fact-check). It's unclear whether linking the review is the builder's job or code's.

**LESSON-one-metre-more-rope (O-1, check stage, lesson v2): passed.** All 3 claims are verified and the order has gone on to the learner stage. The queue was then empty, so my session is closed.

- **c1, circumference = 2πr:** verified. It follows from the definition of π (circumference ÷ diameter) with diameter = 2r.
- **c2, the gap is L ÷ 2π for any radius:** verified. I recomputed it at 0.159155 m for the ball (11 cm), the wheel (35 cm) and the Earth (6,378,137 m). The brief's own check (G1) and the lesson's gap formula in `Demo.tsx` give the same number. The recall question's "about 32 cm" for 2 m is right (0.318 m).
- **c3, the Earth's radius is about 6,378 km:** verified. The WGS 84 semi-major axis is 6,378,137 m, per NIMA TR8350.2 as cited in the EPSG registry.
- **Nothing else a learner sees needs a claim.** The brief's "enough for a cat to crawl under" line is not in the lesson.
- **The zoomed picture is drawn to true scale.** The Earth's ground looks flat because across the window its curve drops by only about 9 nanometres.
- **One advisory note, not a defect:** the small corner icon draws the rope the same distance out for every circle, so it is not to scale. It is a schematic and states nothing, so it isn't a claim.

The record is `company/reviews/one-metre-more-rope/2026-10-22-fact-check-v2.md`.

**Two things that confused me:**
1. A file named `2026-10-22-fact-check.md` already existed, from an earlier fact-check of this lesson that my instructions said not to read. I overwrote it without meaning to, and the claims check refused it because review files cannot be changed. I restored the old file with `git checkout`, without reading it, and saved my record under the new `-v2` name.
2. The claims check takes every status word in a table row as the claim's status. My table had an "Old status" column holding "unverified", so the check saw that disagree with meta.json. I removed the column and the hand-in went through. I put both lessons in `--learned` for the next fact-checker.

Sources:
- [EPSG:4978 (WGS 84)](https://epsg.io/4978)
- [EPSG:7659](https://epsg.io/7659)
- [NGA WGS 84 parameter table (Scribd copy)](https://www.scribd.com/doc/231415084/WGS-84)

I reviewed one lesson, **one-metre-more-rope** (v2), and gave it **launch**. It now moves to the launch stage. No other items were queued, so the session is over.

- **Review file:** `company/reviews/one-metre-more-rope/2026-10-22-learner-knows-pi-times-diameter.md`. I reviewed it as a learner who knows circumference = π × diameter.
- **Why launch:** the Earth frame settles the question on screen. The curve goes flat, and the rope sits at the same 15.9 cm on the same 20 cm ruler as the ball. Every button records "✓ 15.9 cm". The reveal then answers the question a learner would actually have: why the Earth's size doesn't dilute the metre.
- **Two minor notes, neither blocking:**
  - In the walkthrough, Reset was pressed before the reveal. So the reveal's picture shows "gap 0.0 cm" next to text saying the rope was lifted 15.9 cm. The buttons still show 15.9 cm.
  - The reveal says the rope is "2π times the radius", but this learner knows π × diameter. A short "d = 2r" step would close that gap.

**What confused me:** the template needs a `lesson version: v<N>` line, but the walkthrough files never show the version. The only allowed source was `meta.json`. I had worked out my findings from the walkthrough before looking it up, but I checked it before writing the file. I read only its `"version"` line (2), and the review says so. That same `ls` also showed the names of the other review files in that folder; I didn't open any of them.

**LESSON-one-metre-more-rope (O-1): passed launch review with a `go` for v2.** The order has moved on to the ship gates (code runs those). Nothing else was queued, so the session closed itself after this item.

- **Why it's a go:**
  - The walkthrough shows the ball, the wheel and the Earth each giving a 15.9 cm gap against the same 20 cm ruler, which disproves the expected wrong answer on screen.
  - The fact-checker verified all three claims.
  - QA passed on phone and desktop.
  - The simulated learner review gave `Verdict: launch`.
  - Both problems the fact-checker raised on v1 are fixed: the "cat could crawl under" clause is gone, and the recall question now uses a round water tank instead of a running track.
- **Record:** `company/rituals/records/2026-10-22-launch-review-one-metre-more-rope.md`. It lists 7 open objections, each with an owner:
  - the three required ones: no analytics-steward predictions until M7; the accessibility review is advisory and was not run; the learning designer is merged into the builder (F-f).
  - the reveal screen can show the reset picture ("gap 0.0 cm") beside text saying the rope was lifted 15.9 cm.
  - the reveal assumes the learner knows diameter = 2 × radius, which their stated knowledge doesn't spell out.
  - the corner icon is not drawn to scale.
  - `evidence.simulatedLearner` in `meta.json` is empty even though the learner review exists.

**What confused me:** the walkthrough's "Why trust this?" sheet still marks every claim "NOT YET CHECKED". That's because it was recorded about a minute before the second fact-check, and `meta.json` now has all three claims verified. It isn't a defect, but the trust sheet in the walkthrough is out of date compared with `meta.json`. I said so in the record.
